Football fans were exposed to tens of thousands of advertisements for junk food and drinks during the 2026 FIFA World Cup, according to a study by researchers from the universities of Bristol and Oxford. As reported by BBC Sport on Monday, using an artificial intelligence tool, the researchers analysed advertisements visible to television viewers during live play across all 104 matches of the tournament, which was hosted by the United States, Canada and Mexico. The study recorded 65,722 appearances of logos and products from brands classified under UK government criteria as being high in fat, salt or sugar.

news.title: Football Fans Bombarded With 65,000 Junk Food Advertisements During 2026 World Cup
news.lede: A new academic study reveals that audiences viewing the 2026 World Cup were exposed to more than 28 hours of high-fat, salt, and sugar brand advertising. Football fans were exposed to more than 65,000 advertisements for high-fat, salt, and sugar products during the live broadcasts of the 2026 FIFA World Cup, according to a comprehensive new academic study. Researchers from the University of Bristol and the University of Oxford have published findings demonstrating a "constant bombardment" of junk food marketing throughout the tournament, which was jointly hosted by the United States, Canada, and Mexico. To quantify the scale of the advertising exposure, the research team developed a specialized artificial intelligence tool designed to analyse the international television feed for all 104 matches of the expanded tournament.

news.title: CommBank ParaMatildas name squad for IFCPF Women's World Cup title defence
news.lede: The CommBank ParaMatildas will head to Atlanta next month to defend their historic IFCPF Women's World Cup title, with a 10-player squad named by Head Coach Charlotte Ercil. Australia enters the tournament as the reigning world champions and the world’s No. 1-ranked Women’s CP football team, two years after making history in Salou, Spain, by becoming the first Australian national football team to win a World Cup. The ParaMatildas produced a stunning comeback in the 2024 Final, overturning a 2-0 deficit to defeat the USA 6-2 and claim the world title. They have continued to compete at the highest level since, finishing runners-up to the USA at last year’s IFCPF Women’s Intercontinental Cup.

news.title: 'Constant bombardment' - Fans shown 65,000 junk food ads at World Cup
news.lede: This summer's World Cup featured ads promoting an official beverage partner (Coca-Cola), official snack food partner (Lay's), and an official quick-service restaurant sponsor (McDonald's). Football fans were shown a "constant bombardment" of advertisements promoting junk food and drinks during matches at the 2026 Fifa World Cup, according to a new study. Researchers at the University of Bristol and University of Oxford created an AI tool to analyse ads which were visible to television viewers during live play in the tournament's 104 matches, mostly displayed on pitchside advertising boards and around stadiums in the USA, Canada, and Mexico. They found that logos and products for brands that produce junk food and drinks - defined by the UK government as being high in fat, salt or sugar - were displayed 65,722 times in total.

news.title: New Zealand drawn in six-team group for inaugural FIFA U-15 Boys’ World Cup
news.lede: New Zealand have been invited to join 190 other nations at the inaugural FIFA U-15 World Cup & Festival in Azerbaijan in October. The new FIFA tournament will bring together 191 international boys’ teams in Baku, with almost 1,000 matches scheduled across six matchdays from October 24-30, 2026. New Zealand have been drawn in six-team Group T with Madagascar, Mozambique, Puerto Rico, Somalia and Venezuela. Eleven Oceania Football Confederation nations are scheduled to take part.
